title: Umesh Yadav Parts Ways With Vidarbha, Takes NOC to Play for Another State
excerpt: The 38-year-old pacer told The Indian Express the Vidarbha Cricket Association gave him no clarity on his future, prompting his departure ahead of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season.
body:
• Umesh Yadav has ended his long association with Vidarbha, securing a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Vidarbha Cricket Association to represent another state from this season.
  • "I have decided to move on from this season and play for another state. I have got my NOC from Vidarbha Cricket Association," the 38-year-old pacer told The Indian Express.
  • The move follows the VCA's failure to give him clarity about his future with the team, despite his desire to keep playing domestic cricket.
  • The 'Vidarbha Express' — the first player from Vidarbha to represent India, with 170 Test wickets — has not yet announced which state he will turn out for in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy.

Umesh Yadav has severed his long association with Vidarbha. The veteran fast bowler told The Indian Express that he has secured a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Vidarbha Cricket Association (VCA) and will represent another state from this season onward, closing one of the most enduring player-team partnerships in Indian domestic cricket.

"I have decided to move on from this season and play for another state. I have got my NOC from Vidarbha Cricket Association."

— Umesh Yadav, speaking to The Indian Express

Why he walked away

The decision, Yadav indicated, was driven by a lack of communication from the state association. He had asked the VCA for clarity on his future with the team but received no proper response, leaving him with little choice but to seek a fresh start elsewhere. He recently turned out in the Vidarbha Premier League and performed well, and he wanted to play more cricket for the state — but the uncertainty from the association forced his hand.

Vidarbha are the defending Ranji Trophy champions, having lifted the title in the 2024-25 season — their third championship after breakthrough triumphs in 2017-18 and 2018-19. Yadav's departure therefore carries an edge: one of the side's most decorated senior pros is walking out of a title-winning dressing room because he was kept guessing about his place in it.

The 'Vidarbha Express' and a storied home career

Yadav's ties to Vidarbha run deeper than most domestic associations ever get to claim. Born in Nagpur in 1987, he became the first player from Vidarbha to represent India when he made his Test debut in 2011. Over 57 Tests, he claimed 170 wickets at an average of 30.95, earning a reputation as one of India's most consistent purveyors of raw pace across 2010s and early 2020s.

His limited-overs numbers are equally substantial: 106 wickets in 75 ODIs and 12 in nine T20Is, before he was phased out of white-ball contention after 2022. Through it all, Yadav remained famously loyal to his home state. When India duty allowed, he turned up for Vidarbha without fuss — famously producing career-best first-class figures of 7 for 48 against Kerala in the 2018-19 Ranji Trophy semifinal, a 12-wicket match haul that helped power Vidarbha toward a second straight title. During the following season's title defence, he took 23 wickets in just three matches at a stunning average of 12.26.

An uncertain road back — but not done yet

Yadav has not played for India since the 2023 World Test Championship final against Australia at The Oval, where he managed 2 for 131 across both innings in a heavy defeat. Since then, the national selectors have moved on, favouring a younger generation of fast bowlers led by Mohammed Siraj and the next wave behind Jasprit Bumrah. His last competitive outing for Vidarbha came in November last year.

None of that has dimmed his appetite for the game. After undergoing leg surgery earlier this year and going unsold in the IPL 2025 auction, Yadav has been blunt about where he stands. "After that, I had my leg surgery. Till I feel I can clock 140 kmph, I will bowl. When I won't be able to bowl, I'll quit cricket myself," he told InsideSport. The departure from Vidarbha, then, is less a farewell than a relocation — a 38-year-old still convinced he has wickets left in him, refusing to be parked on the bench.

"Till I feel I can clock 140 kmph, I will bowl. When I won't be able to bowl, I'll quit cricket myself. I won't have to tell this to anyone."

— Umesh Yadav, on his playing future

What's next

The immediate question is which state Yadav will represent in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy. With the domestic season already underway through the Duleep Trophy and the Irani Cup up next, an announcement is expected before the Ranji campaign begins. For Vidarbha, meanwhile, the task is to defend their crown without the 'Vidarbha Express' leading the attack — a test of how far their development pipeline has truly come since that first title in 2018.

For diaspora fans who watched him burst onto the scene as the boy from Nagpur who bowled genuine pace without ever attending a formal academy, this chapter is bittersweet: the end of a hometown story, but proof that the fire to compete still burns.
